summary: Descendants and the spouse are guaranteed half of their intestate share, with a smaller share for other close relatives. There is no trust law, and the Hague Trusts Convention is not in force. Foundations are limited to public-benefit use.
reserved_share: Descendants, adoptees and spouse: 1/2 of the intestate share; parents and other heirs a smaller share (1/3); Law on Inheritance (OG 47/96). Article numbers not confirmed.
foreign_law_note: The 2007 Law on Private International Law governs succession; whether a foreign national may choose their national law was not confirmed.
trust_note: No trust law. Foundations exist under the Law on Associations and Foundations (2010), mainly for public benefit.
open_questions: Statute article numbers and exact fractions for forced heirs outside descendants and spouse were not read in the primary text; confirm in the official gazette.
Whether a foreign national resident may choose a law for their estate under the current private international law act was not confirmed.
A draft civil code may change forced heirship.
